DIRECTION ONLY. No weeks-level percentile was found in a source opened this session; both cited studies were only reachable through search-engine summaries, not opened directly (see wars-sources.md). Both report that third-party/foreign military intervention is associated with LONGER civil-war duration, not shorter, especially when the intervention favors one side alone or when interveners split evenly across both sides. Recommendation: treat a civil war seeded with active foreign troop involvement as sitting at or above the non_coup_non_revolution median (row above, ~470wk), not below it, until a harder number is sourced.
